meta.title: Kanso — a project, end to end, mirrored to Notion
meta.description: Kanso runs a project end to end — teams, projects, tickets, cycles, a roadmap, a timeline with dependencies, workload — and keeps the documents that explain it alongside. Self-hosted, AGPL-3.0.
hero.title: Kanso runs a project end to end — teams, projects, tickets, cycles, a roadmap, a timeline with dependencies, workload — and keeps the documents that explain it alongside.
hero.lead: Everyone who does not open it reads the same data in Notion.
hero.statuses: A team names its own statuses — six to begin with, backlog to canceled, and it renames, reorders, adds and removes them. One keystroke each, the same words in the list, the board and the timeline.
walk.title: Five screens, in the order you meet them
walk.lead: A project, a ticket, then the same tickets read three ways.
step.project.title: Create a project
step.project.caption: A team owns its tickets; a project groups them across the team and carries a lead, a status and dates. Cycles and the roadmap read from the same rows.
step.project.alt: A project in Kanso, with its lead, its status and its dates.
step.ticket.title: Create a ticket
step.ticket.caption: c from anywhere, e to rename in place, 1–6 for your team's first six statuses and ⇧s to pick any of them by name. The ticket takes a short per-team identifier — KAN-1, then KAN-2 — allocated inside the insert.
step.ticket.alt: A ticket in Kanso, with its identifier, its status and its assignee.
step.timeline.title: Read it as a timeline
step.timeline.caption: Bars, dependencies between them, and a warning when two overlap. One scoped query, drawn as time.
step.timeline.alt: The Kanso timeline: bars over weeks, with arrows between dependent tickets.
step.board.title: Read it as a board
step.board.caption: The same query, drawn as one column per status the team has. Dragging a card changes the status and nothing else. Scoped wider than one team, the columns become the five meanings both vocabularies share, and a drop writes each card's own team's word.
step.board.alt: The Kanso board: one column per status, with ticket cards.
step.assigned.title: Read it as one person's list
step.assigned.caption: The same query again, filtered to an assignee and kept as a saved view. List, board and timeline are three dispositions of one query, not three features to keep in step — which is also why workload per person is a reading of the same rows and not a report.
step.assigned.alt: The Kanso list filtered to one assignee, grouped by status.
pillars.title: Four things, in this order
pillar.project.title: A whole project, not a task list.
pillar.project.body: Cycles, a roadmap, a timeline that knows its dependencies and warns about overlap, workload per person.
pillar.document.title: The document sits next to the work.
pillar.document.body: Notion pages are referenced by projects and tickets, many-to-many on both sides. The page that explains a decision hangs off the work it decided, instead of being filed in a second tool.
pillar.keyboard.title: At the keyboard.
pillar.keyboard.body: j/k to move, 1–6 for your team's own statuses, ⌘K for the palette, / to filter. The same keys in all three views.
pillar.readers.title: Nobody else has to learn Kanso.
pillar.readers.body: Connect Notion and Kanso feeds four databases. The people who only need to follow along build their own views there and never open Kanso.
notion.title: Both directions, and only one of them is a loop
notion.out.title: Outbound, continuously
notion.out.body: Every write enqueues a job in the same transaction, and a worker pushes it into four databases. Readers filter, group and chart them in Notion the way they already do, and never open Kanso. Postgres stays the source of truth; Notion catches up, and Kanso stays usable while it is down.
notion.in.title: Inbound, once
notion.in.body: Arrive with six months of tickets already in Notion and the import adopts them: it lists the databases it can see, you say which team each one becomes, and it copies the pages in. Once. Afterwards tickets are created in Kanso — a page created in Notion later is logged and left where it is, and the poller only carries scalar fields back: title, status, priority, dates, archived. Assignees and relations stay Kanso's.
notion.landing: One door to move in, one source of truth to live in.
run.title: Two commands, on your own machine
run.env: cp .env.example .env      # fill in OIDC credentials, or set KANSO_AUTH_MODE=dev
run.wizard: First launch opens a setup wizard. You create the owner account with an email and a password, then — if you want to — link Notion, enable Google sign-in and pick a theme. Every step after the account is skippable and reopenable from settings, so you can be filing tickets in under a minute.
run.optional: Notion is optional. With no token every write still enqueues a sync job and a no-op client completes it: the queue and the retry machinery run, and nothing leaves the machine.

closing.title: It runs the project. Everyone else reads it in Notion.
closing.body: One instance, your Postgres, your Notion token or none at all. Nothing to sign up for and nothing to send us — there is no telemetry to switch off.
footer.captures: The captures are taken from the running application by a test that waits for each screen, so a moved screen breaks the script instead of photographing the wrong thing.
